parts.text:
Using calculus, find the coordinates of the stationary point on the curve with equation
$y = 2x + 3 + \dfrac{8}{x^2}, \quad x>0$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2-16x^{-3}$ M1 A1
$2-16x^{-3}=0$ so $x^{-3}=$ or $x^3=$, or $2-16x^{-3}=0$ so $x=2$ M1
$x=2$ only (after correct derivative) A1
$y=2\times\text{"2"}+3+\dfrac{8}{\text{"2"}^2}$ M1
$=9$ A1
Notes: 1st M1: At least one term differentiated (not integrated) correctly, so $2x\to 2$, or $\dfrac{8}{x^2}\to -16x^{-3}$, or $3\to 0$. A1: this answer or equivalent e.g. $2-\dfrac{16}{x^3}$. 2nd M1: Sets $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ to 0, and solves to give $x^3=$ value or $x^{-3}=$ value (or states $x=2$ with no working following correctly stated $2-16x^{-3}=0$). A1: $x=2$ cso (if $x=-2$ is included this is A0 here). 3rd M1: Attempts to substitute their positive $x$ (found from attempt to differentiate) into $y=2x+3+\dfrac{8}{x^2}, x>0$; or may be implied by $y=9$ or correct follow through from their positive $x$. A1: 9 cao (does not need to be written as coordinates) (ignore the extra $(-2,1)$ here).

parts.text:
Find the first 4 terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of
$\left(2-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^8$
giving each term in its simplest form.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: $\left(2-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^8 = 2^8 + \binom{8}{1}2^7\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right) + \binom{8}{2}2^6\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^2 + \binom{8}{3}2^5\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^3$
First term of 256 B1
$\left(^8C_1\times\ldots\times x\right)+\left(^8C_2\times\ldots\times x^2\right)+\left(^8C_3\times\ldots\times x^3\right)$ M1
$=(256)-512x+448x^2-224x^3$ A1, A1
Way 2: $\left(2-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^8 = 2^8\left(1-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)^8 = 2^8\left(1+\binom{8}{1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)+\binom{8}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)^2+\binom{8}{3}\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)^3\right)$; scheme is applied exactly as before except in special case below.
Notes: B1: the first term should be 256 in their expansion. M1: two binomial coefficients must be correct and must be with the correct power of $x$. Accept $^8C_1$ or $\binom{8}{1}$ or 8 as a coefficient, and $^8C_2$ or $\binom{8}{2}$ or 28 as another. Pascal's triangle may be used to establish coefficients. A1: any two of the final three terms correct (but allow +- instead of -). A1: all three of the final three terms correct and simplified (deduct last mark for $+-512x$ and $+-224x^3$ in the series; also deduct last mark for the three terms correct but unsimplified; accept answers without + signs, can be listed with commas or appear on separate lines). The common error $\left(2-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)^8 = 256+\binom{8}{1}2^7\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x\right)+\binom{8}{2}2^6\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right)+\binom{8}{3}2^5\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}x^3\right)$ would earn B1, M1, A0, A0. Ignore extra terms involving higher powers. Condone terms in reverse order i.e. $=-224x^3+448x^2-512x+(256)$. *In Way 2 the error $=2\left(1+\binom{8}{1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)+\binom{8}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)^2+\binom{8}{3}\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)^3\right)$ giving $=2-4x+\dfrac{7}{2}x^2-\dfrac{7}{4}x^3$ is a special case B0, M1, A1, A0 i.e. 2/4.

questions.stem:
$\mathrm{f}(x) = ax^3 - 11x^2 + bx + 4$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
When $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(x-3)$ the remainder is 55
When $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is divided by $(x+1)$ the remainder is $-9$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: Attempting $\mathrm{f}(\pm 1)$ or $\mathrm{f}(\pm 3)$ M1
Sets $\mathrm{f}(3)=55$ i.e. $27a-99+3b+4=55$ A1
Sets $\mathrm{f}(-1)=-9$ i.e. $-a-11-b+4=-9$ A1
$a=\ldots/b=\ldots$ M1
$a=6$ and $b=-4$ A1cao
Way 2: Divides by $(x-3)$ and reaches remainder or divides by $(x+1)$ and reaches remainder M1
Sets remainder $=55$: $27a-99+3b+4=55$ A1
Sets remainder $=-9$: $-a-11-b+4=-9$ A1
$a=\ldots/b=\ldots$ M1
$a=6$ and $b=-4$ A1cao
Notes (Way 1): M1: attempting $\mathrm{f}(\pm 1)$ or $\mathrm{f}(\pm 3)$ — with numbers substituted into expression. A1: for applying $\mathrm{f}(3)$ correctly and setting the result equal to 55 (see correct equation then isw). A1: for applying $\mathrm{f}(-1)$ correctly and setting the result equal to $-9$ (see correct equation then isw). M1: solve simultaneously to obtain a value for either $a$ or $b$ (may make slip). A1: both values correct — this could imply M1 if no working. Or Way 2: M1: long division by $(x-3)$ or $(x+1)$. A1, A1: correct remainders put equal to 55 or $-9$ respectively. M1, A1: as in Way 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $(3x+2)$ is a factor of $\mathrm{f}(x)$,
(b) factorise $\mathrm{f}(x)$ completely.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\mathrm{f}(x) = (3x+2)(2x^2-5x+2)$ or $\left(x+\dfrac{2}{3}\right)(6x^2-15x+6)$ M1 A1
$=(3x+2)(x-2)(2x-1)$ or $=(3x+2)(2-x)(1-2x)$ M1 A1
Notes: 1st M1: attempting to divide a multiple of their cubic by $(3x+2)$ or $\left(x+\dfrac{2}{3}\right)$ leading to a 3TQ beginning with the correct term, usually $\dfrac{a}{3}x^2$. A1: for either $(2x^2-5x+2)$ after division by $(3x+2)$ or $(6x^2-15x+6)$ after division by $\left(x+\dfrac{2}{3}\right)$. 2nd M1: for a valid attempt to factorise their quadratic. 2nd A1: for any equivalent correct answer and needs all three factors together. As shown in scheme, apply isw if candidate continues to "solve" and give $x=\ldots$

questions.stem: The first three terms of a geometric series are $4p$, $(3p+15)$ and $(5p+20)$ respectively, where $p$ is a positive constant.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
$a=4p$, $ar=(3p+15)$ and $ar^2=5p+20$ B1
(So $r=$) $\dfrac{5p+20}{3p+15}=\dfrac{3p+15}{4p}$ or $4p(5p+20)=(3p+15)^2$ or equivalent M1
See $(3p+15)^2=9p^2+90p+225$ M1
$20p^2+80p=9p^2+90p+225 \Rightarrow 11p^2-10p-225=0$ * A1*
Notes: B1: correct statement (needs all three terms) — this may be omitted and implied by correct statement in $p$ only as candidates may use geometric mean, or may use ratio of terms being equal and give a correct line 2 without line 1 (this would earn the B1M1 immediately). M1: valid attempt to eliminate $a$ and $r$ and to obtain equation in $p$ only. M1: correct expansion of $(3p+15)^2=9p^2+90p+225$. A1 cso: no incorrect work seen; the printed answer is obtained. NB those who show $p=5$ in part (a) obtain no credit for this.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
$(p-5)(11p+45)$ so $p=$ M1
$p=5$ only (after rejecting $-45/11$) A1
N.B. Special case $p=5$ can be verified in (b) (1 mark only): $11\times 5^2-10\times 5-225 = 275-50-225=0$ M1A0
Notes: M1: attempt to solve quadratic by usual methods (factorisation, completion of square or formula); must appear in part (b) — not part (a). A1: 5 only and $-45/11$ should be seen and rejected or $(11p+45)$ seen and statement $p>0$.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the common ratio of this series.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\dfrac{3\times 5+15}{4\times 5}$ or $\dfrac{5\times 5+20}{3\times 5+15}$ M1
$r=\dfrac{3}{2}$ A1
Notes: M1: substitutes $p=5$ completely and attempt ratio (correct way up). A1: 1.5 or any equivalent.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Find the sum of the first ten terms of the series, giving your answer to the nearest integer.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$S_{10}=\dfrac{20\left(1-\left(\text{"}\frac{3}{2}\text{"}\right)^{10}\right)}{1-\left(\text{"}\frac{3}{2}\text{"}\right)}$ M1A1ft
$(=2266.601568\ldots) = 2267$ A1
Notes: M1: use of correct formula with $n=10$, $a$ and/or $r$ may still be in terms of $p$. A1ft: correct expression ft on their $r$ only — must have $a=20$ and power $=10$ here. A1: 2267 (accept awrt 2267).

questions.stem: Given that $\log_3 x = a$, find in terms of $a$,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: $\log_3(9x)=\log_3 9+\log_3 x$ M1
$=2+a$ A1
Way 2: $\log_3(9x)=\log_3 3^{a+2}$ M1
$=2+a$ A1
Notes: Way 1: M1: use of $\log(ab)=\log(a)+\log(b)$; A1: must be $a+2$ or $2+a$. Way 2: uses $x=3^a$ to give $\log_3(9x)=\log_3 3^{a+2}$; A1 for $a+2$ or $2+a$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) $\log_3\left(\dfrac{x^5}{81}\right)$
giving each answer in its simplest form.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: $\log_3\left(\dfrac{x^5}{81}\right)=\log_3 x^5-\log_3 81$ M1
$\log x^5=5\log x$ or $\log 81=4\log 3$ or $\log 81=4$ M1
$=5a-4$ A1 cso
Way 2: $=\log_3\dfrac{3^{5a}}{3^4}$ M1
$=\log_3 3^{5a-4}$ M1
$=5a-4$ A1 cso
Notes: Way 1: M1: use of $\log(a/b)=\log(a)-\log(b)$; M1: use of $n\log(a)=\log(a)^n$; A1: no errors seen. Way 2: M1: use of correct powers of 3 in numerator and denominator; M1: subtracts powers; A1: no errors seen.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Solve, for $x$,
$\log_3(9x)+\log_3\left(\dfrac{x^5}{81}\right)=3$
giving your answer to 4 significant figures.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Method 1: $\Rightarrow 2+a+5a-4=3$ M1
$\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{5}{6}$ A1
$\Rightarrow x=3^{5/6}$ or $\log_{10}x=a\log_{10}3$ so $x=$ M1
$x=2.498$ or awrt A1
Method 2: $\log_3\left(9x\cdot\dfrac{x^5}{81}\right)=(3 \text{ or } \log 27)$ M1
$\log_3\left(\dfrac{x^6}{9}\right)=3$ or $\log 27$ A1
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{x^6}{9}=3^3 \Rightarrow x^6=3^5 \Rightarrow x=$ M1
$x=2.498$ or awrt A1
If $x=-2.498$ appears as well or instead this is A0.

(2)

(4)

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows the graph of $y=x^2+2x+2$ and the line $y=10$.
The line with equation $y=10$ cuts the curve with equation $y=x^2+2x+2$ at the points $A$ and $B$ as shown in Figure 1. The figure is not drawn to scale.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find by calculation the $x$-coordinate of $A$ and the $x$-coordinate of $B$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$x^2+2x+2=10 \Rightarrow x^2+2x-8=0$ (so $(x+4)(x-2)=0$) $\Rightarrow x=\ldots$ M1
$x=-4, 2$ A1
Notes: M1: set the curve equation equal to 10 and collect terms; solves quadratic to $x=\ldots$. A1 cao: both values correct — allow $A=-4$, $B=2$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The shaded region $R$ is bounded by the line with equation $y=10$ and the curve as shown in Figure 1.
(b) Use calculus to find the exact area of $R$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: $\int(x^2+2x+2)\,dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{2x^2}{2}+2x(+C)$ M1A1A1
$\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{2x^2}{2}+2x\right]_{\text{"-4"}}^{\text{"2"}} = \left(\dfrac{8}{3}+\dfrac{8}{2}+4\right)-\left(-\dfrac{64}{3}+\dfrac{32}{2}-8\right)$ $(=24)$ M1
Rectangle: $10\times(2-(-4))=60$ B1 cao
$R = \text{"60"}-\text{"24"}$ M1
$=36$ A1
Way 2: $\int(8-x^2-2x)\,dx = 8x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{2x^2}{2}(+C)$ M1A1ftA1
$\left[8x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\dfrac{2x^2}{2}\right]_{\text{"-4"}}^{\text{"2"}} = (16-\tfrac{8}{3}-4)-(-32+\tfrac{64}{3}-16)$ $=(9.3-(-26.7))$ M1
Implied by final answer of 36 after correct work B1
$10-(x^2+2x+2)=8-x^2-2x$, $=36$ M1, A1
Notes: M1: one correct integration; A1: two correct integrations (ft slips subtracting in Way 2); A1: all 3 terms correct (penalise subtraction errors here in Way 2); M1: substitute their limits from (a) into the integrated function and subtract (either way round); B1: Way 1: find area under the line by integration or area of rectangle — should be 60 here (no follow through); Way 2: (implied by final correct answer in second method); M1: subtract one area from the other (implied by subtraction of functions in second method) — award even after differentiation; A1: must be 36 not $-36$. Special case 1: combines both methods, uses Way 2 integration, but continues after reaching "36" to subtract "36" from rectangle giving answer as "24" — this loses final M1 A1. Special case 2: integrates $(x^2+2x-8)$ between limits $-4$ and 2 to get $-36$ and then changes sign and obtains 36; do not award final A mark — so M1A1A1M1B1M1A0. If the answer is left as $-36$, then M1A1A1M1B0M1A0. N.B. allow full marks for modulus used earlier in working e.g. $\left|\int_{-4}^{2} x^2+2x-2\,dx\right|-\int_{-4}^{2}10\,dx$

questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows the design for a triangular garden $ABC$ where $AB=7$ m, $AC=13$ m and $BC=10$ m.
Given that angle $BAC = \theta$ radians,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: $10^2=7^2+13^2-2\times 7\times 13\cos\theta$ or $\cos\theta=\dfrac{7^2+13^2-10^2}{2\times 7\times 13}$ M1
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{59}{91}$ or $\cos\theta=\dfrac{7^2+13^2-10^2}{2\times 7\times 13}$ or $\cos\theta=0.6483$ or $0.8644$ A1 o.e
$(\theta=0.8653789549\ldots)=0.865$ * (to 3 dp) A1* cso
Way 2: uses $\cos\theta=\dfrac{x}{7}$, where $7^2-x^2=10^2-(13-x)^2$ and finds $x$ ($=59/13$) M1
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{59}{91}$ A1, A1
and $(\theta=0.8653789549\ldots)=0.865$ * (to 3 dp) — as in Way 1
Notes: M1: use correct cosine formula in any form; A1: give a value for $\cos\theta$; NB $\cos\theta=\dfrac{7^2+13^2-10^2}{2\times 7\times 13}$ earns M1A1; A1: deduce and state the printed answer $\theta=0.865$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The point $D$ lies on $AC$ such that $BD$ is an arc of the circle centre $A$, radius 7 m.
The shaded region $S$ is bounded by the arc $BD$ and the lines $BC$ and $DC$. The shaded region $S$ will be sown with grass seed, to make a lawned area.
Given that 50 g of grass seed are needed for each square metre of lawn,
(b) find the amount of grass seed needed, giving your answer to the nearest 10 g.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:

Area sector $ABD=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 7^2\times 0.865$ or $\dfrac{49.6}{360}\times\pi\times 7^2$ M1
$=34.6$ (triangle) or $21.2$ (Sector) A1
Area of $S=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 13\times 7\sin 0.865-\dfrac{1}{2}\times 7^2\times 0.865$ ($=13.4$) M1 A1
(Amount of seed $=$) $13.4\times 50=670$g or $680$g (need one of these two answers) M1 A1
Notes: M1: uses correct method for area of the correct triangle i.e. $ABC$; M1: uses correct method for the area of the sector; A1: this is earned for one of the correct answers, may be implied if these answers are not calculated but the final answer is correct with no errors (or shaded area is 13.4 or 13.5); M1: their area of triangle $ABC$ minus area of sector (may have $kr^2\theta$ but not $k\theta$); A1: correct expression or awrt 13.4 or 13.5 (may be implied by final answer); M1: multiply their previous answer by 50; A1: 670g or 680g (there is an argument for rounding answer up to provide enough seed). giving your answers to 1 decimal place.
You must show clearly how you obtained your answers.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:

$(3\cos x-1)(2\cos x-3)=0$ implies $\cos x=$ M1
$\cos x=\dfrac{1}{3}, \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ A1
$x=70.5$ B1
$x=360-\text{"70.5"}$ M1
$x=289.5$ A1 cao
